newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand welcomes Yankee bond pricing.
newsitem.headline: Thailand welcomes Yankee bond pricing.

text.p: Analysts in Thailand on Friday welcomed a good U.S. market reception of Thailand's $600 million Yankee bond, calling it a successful debut of its major sovereign debt issue.
"The issue got a very relatively cheap and conservative pricing especially for Thailand's first foray into the Yankee bond market," said Brett Williams of Krungthai Thanakit Plc.
The 10-year Thai issue was priced late on Thursday at 90 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, and the size of the issue was raised to $600 million from $500 million.

A currency dealer at Hongkong and Shanghai Bank described the 90 basis point pricing as moderate, saying it proved that Thailand's ratings downgrade by Moody's Investors Service earlier this week did not have overly negative consequences for the country.

Prateep Leelakittikul of Hongkong Bank said the market is waiting for details on why the issue size was increased but it was clear that funds raised by the issue would be channeled to finance state enterprises and were unlikely to be used by the government.
"The Thai government itself does not need any foreign funding as it still aims to meet its balanced fiscal budget target this year," he said.
Another dealer at Bank of Ayudhya Plc said the bigger Thai Yankee bond issue was intended for testing market reaction in order to gauge any damage from the Moody's downgrading of Thai debt ratings.

Moody's on Wednesday cut Thailand's foreign currency ceilings for bonds and bank deposits to A3 from A2. It also cut senior debt and deposit ratings of five Thai banks to the same investment grade rating.
